text.p: Moscow is considering bidding to host the 2008 Olympic Games, the mayor of the Russian capital said on Sunday.
"It think that Boris Yeltsin will support such a decision," said Yuri Luzhkov, a dynamic organiser who makes little secret of his ambition to succeed the Russian president.

If Yeltsin did back Moscow's Olympic bid, it would be a kick in the teeth for Russia's second city and former capital, St Petersburg. Moscow's rival down the centuries, the Baltic port's bid for the 2004 Games failed to make the shortlist in March.

St Petersburg officials, convinced their decaying baroque city can make the grade, vowed at the time to bid again. The Kremlin is unlikely to back two candidates and without federal cash St Petersburg would be unable to make an impact.

Moscow's 10 million population is twice that of the "northern capital" and it has maintained standards of living well above those elsewhere in the country in the midst of the economic collapse that followed the end of the Soviet system.

Moscow staged the Olympics in 1980 when the communist authorities restocked shops to shorten food queues and banished social misfits from the capital. The Games were marred by a U.S. boycott in protest at the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
Several U.S. cities are contemplating bids for the 2008 Games, including San Francisco, New York and Boston, along with unsuccessful candidates for 2004, such as Rio de Janeiro and Seville.
